pivot_dispositions.DOS-M00-000: The gate still exists but now must freeze a hosted-LiveView-plus-anonymous-browser-storage architecture instead of an on-device one.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M00-002: Becomes the browser-MVP architecture ADR: Fly.io as the sole app host, Netlify as static-content-only, browser storage as the sole personal-data store, and the hydration protocol as the ratified seam.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M00-004: The dual-store idea survives but splits across a boundary: prove a read-only server-side catalog SQLite plus a client IndexedDB user store with its own forward-only versioning, not two on-device Ecto repos.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M01-000: Offline-safe becomes reproducible and deployable — the platform target is a container on Fly, not a signed device package.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M01-001: Drop Xcode/Android SDK/Gradle/Mob pins; keep Elixir/OTP/Phoenix/esbuild/Tailwind/SQLite pins and add Docker base image and flyctl version pinning.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M01-002: The platform adapter port is no longer a native bridge but a browser-storage port whose only implementation is the JS hook plus IndexedDB adapter, with a test double for server-side tests.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M01-003: CatalogRepo stays server-side Ecto/SQLite unchanged; UserRepo stops being an Ecto schema and becomes an IndexedDB object-store layout with an independent version line.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M01-005: The shell becomes a hosted Phoenix app bound to a public interface behind Fly proxy with TLS and origin checks — replacing the loopback/WebView handshake — while the separate static Netlify support-site half carries over as written.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M01-006: The device matrix becomes a browser/engine matrix, and release evidence becomes deploy evidence (image digest, catalog version, release ID) rather than store-build artifacts.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M02-000: Freeze a responsive web interaction model (URLs, back button, refresh, tab focus) instead of a native mobile one; the language/content contract carries over intact.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M02-001: Routes become real shareable URLs with browser history, refresh, and deep-link semantics, and every flow must define its pre-hydration entry state.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M02-002: Replace native platform components and OS accessibility APIs with a responsive web design system and a WCAG 2.2 AA contract verified against browser assistive technology.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M02-003: First run now means hydration-from-empty rather than bundled-catalog verification, and the privacy copy must say this browser on this device, explicitly warn that clearing site data destroys the record, and cover private-browsing and storage-blocked cases.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M02-004: Search is served by a server-side query layer rather than a local database, so the spec must add network-latency, request-failure, and offline states that the offline design never needed.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M02-005: The one-vehicle-now/multi-vehicle-later product shape is unchanged, but the tabs navigation direction must be respecified as a web navigation pattern.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M02-008: Delete the OS permission-prompt and notification-delivery UX; the MVP specifies in-app due/overdue presentation only, plus honest copy that nothing arrives while the app is closed.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M03-001: The rights analysis must now evaluate serving data over a public web service, which is a materially different redistribution mode from shipping rows inside a signed binary and may change the answer for individual sources.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M04-000: The epic splits along the new boundary: read-only catalog persistence on the server, and anonymous personal-record persistence in the browser.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M04-001: The ADR must now cover server CatalogRepo plus browser UserStore plus the hydration/mutation protocol, and state as a MUST that no personal row is ever written server-side.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M04-003: The logical model and its invariants survive but must be expressed as IndexedDB object stores and indexes enforced in the client adapter and re-validated server-side on hydration, since SQL constraints are no longer available.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M04-005: Becomes a browser storage adapter providing transactional IndexedDB semantics, with the server holding the same data only in socket assigns for the session lifetime.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M04-006: Split into server catalog boot at application start and client store open-and-hydrate on LiveView mount; the native durable-file placement requirement drops.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M04-007: Becomes an IndexedDB onupgradeneeded forward-only schema upgrade executed on connection open, with no rollback path and explicit quota/eviction/abort handling.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M04-008: Becomes atomic activation of a new catalog version within a Fly release (no half-swapped reads, version pinning, rollback); the bundle-copy mechanics park with the native re-entry set.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M04-009: Export becomes a generated file download and import a file-picker upload via browser File APIs instead of native share sheets, and erasure clears IndexedDB and localStorage — this is now the ONLY portability mechanism and rises in priority.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M04-010: Replace physical-device budgets with browser/engine conformance and server budgets, and add quota-exhaustion, eviction, private-browsing, and multi-tab conformance cases that did not exist on device.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M05-000: Local-only, offline becomes hosted, anonymous browser storage, connectivity required for catalog; the single-vehicle scope boundary is unchanged.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M05-001: Integration now means wiring server catalog reads to hydrated client state held in assigns, rather than wiring two co-located on-device repos.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M05-002: Search is a server query over the hosted catalog, so the local-query latency budget becomes a network-plus-server p95 budget and request-failure states become mandatory.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M05-003: Every create and edit commits through the pushEvent then hook then IndexedDB round trip and is not shown as saved until the hook acknowledges.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M05-004: Same write-path change, plus the append-only audit guarantees must be enforced in the client adapter because there is no server transaction to rely on.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M05-005: The dashboard must render a determinate pre-hydration state, must not flash a false empty garage, and must never imply the record is backed up on the server it is loaded from.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M05-006: Becomes the Fly.io deploy-and-boot contract — reproducible image, pinned toolchain, health check before traffic, release manifest binding app/catalog/storage-schema versions — with icons, splash screens, and signed native packages carved out to the native re-entry set.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M05-007: Same envelope, checksum, preview-before-import, and replace semantics, delivered through browser download/upload with added guidance that browser data-clearing is the realistic loss scenario.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M06-000: The forecasting half survives intact; the notification half narrows to in-app due/overdue state, with OS delivery moved to the native re-entry and Web Push to a spike.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M06-002: The recurring prompt has no background scheduler in a browser, so recurring sampling must be respecified as an on-visit prompt driven by elapsed time since the last sample.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M06-005: Keep the desired-reminder plan as a pure domain output rendered as in-app due/overdue state; the mob_notify delivery half splits out into a new deferred native issue.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M06-007: Becomes in-app reminder preferences plus a due-state correctness gate; the OS delivery-reliability portion of the gate moves to the native re-entry.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M07-000: Store release becomes public web launch on the custom domain; the hardening and closed-beta structure carries over.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M07-001: The threat model changes fundamentally — a public internet-facing server replaces a loopback listener — and must now cover socket/origin abuse, transient personal data in assigns, log and error-report redaction, and a provable absence of personal-data tables.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M07-002: Native platform accessibility APIs are replaced by WCAG 2.2 AA conformance verified across a named browser and assistive-technology matrix, including keyboard-only desktop use that the mobile bar never covered.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M07-003: Battery and native-memory budgets are replaced by page-load, time-to-hydrated, LiveView round-trip latency, server memory-per-socket, and IndexedDB footprint budgets.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M07-004: The matrix becomes browser/engine/OS instead of iOS/Android, notification rows are removed, and storage-eviction, quota, private-browsing, multi-tab, and reconnect rows are added.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M07-005: Signed native store builds become signed/attested container images with reproducible provenance and an immutable Fly release identifier.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M07-006: Beta distribution moves from TestFlight/Play tracks to an unlisted staging hostname or invite link, and defect intake must not collect browser storage contents.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M07-007: Store records, screenshots, ratings, and review notes drop; the deliverable becomes staged Fly deploys, custom-domain cutover, canary smoke checks, monitoring, and a rehearsed rollback.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M08-000: Remains post-MVP, but multi-vehicle now means multi-vehicle in browser storage and catalog operations now means server-side catalog releases.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M08-001: The vehicle-scoped schema it activates is the IndexedDB object-store layout, and enabling it requires a client storage schema-version migration rather than an Ecto migration.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M08-002: Respecify the tabbed pattern as an accessible web navigation pattern with real URLs per vehicle.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M08-003: Per-vehicle isolation must be enforced in the client store and in the hydration payload shape, since there is no server-side row scoping to rely on.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M08-005: The client-verified pack and trust root become build-and-deploy-time signing and verification of the catalog artifact, since the browser client never downloads a pack.
pivot_dispositions.DOS-M08-006: Content-addressed immutable publish, canary verification, and pointer rollback survive as concepts but target the Fly catalog release channel; Netlify retains only static content.
